title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 22)
summary: Final Meditations episode: a collection of favorite passages on acting without seeking recognition, confronting your own vices, personal responsibility, not postponing self-improvement, and not letting sickness define you. He announces the next books: Enchiridion, Discourses, Seneca, then Nietzsche.
claims: Don't do things to be praised; act for what you judge to be good and for the community, and progress follows
Strength of character is standing in a room of a thousand people who disagree with you and being completely untouched
Rather than fleeing other people's vices, reject the vice in yourself; a vice is a parasite, not you, and the power to repress it is what makes you human
Do good without seeking reward or reputation; chasing kickbacks corrupts you until you only do good for the kickback
Modern moral relativism is mostly contrarianism: deconstructing everything without purpose or answers
You can ignore a vice or fight it, but complaining is passive and feeds it
Stoic principles are innate biological drives; you don't need to read the book to live them
Changing your mind through your own judgment is no loss of freedom; dropping fanboy behavior means being critical of everyone, him included
Take 100% personal responsibility at all times; giving it up is choosing your own chains
Pleasure is not worth pursuing and pain is not to be avoided; hedonism pleases the body, not the self
'I'll start tomorrow' means never, in morals and in training: start now
In speech, content comes before elegance; be truthful and intellectually honest
Blue pill is ignorance, black pill knows but refuses to act (pathetic nihilism), red pill knows, sees and acts
Accepting your present state is what allows you to move forward; self-hatred keeps you stuck
Don't let illness or weakness become your identity, and refuse to be coddled by others, which keeps you weak
Next in the series: Epictetus' Enchiridion, then the Discourses, Seneca's On the Happy Life, then Nietzsche
